transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 15:30 PDT | Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Samira Kline (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Mark Delaney (CTO, Tidecrest), Asha Iyer (ML Eng), Ben Carter (SRE), Jules Park (Security).

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Goal: show parity path for switching from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API; map endpoints, surface compatibility gotchas, and outline POC and benchmarks.
- Key asks from Tidecrest: preserve latency 95p under 150ms for 4k token requests, KMS integration, VPC peering/on-prem option for sensitive data.
- Next: pricing + runbook, perf benchmark, POC checklist.

Topics: parity mapping, streaming differences, KV cache behavior, batching tradeoffs, quantization options, private deployment and KMS, security docs (SOC2), POC timeline.

00:00 Samira Kline: "Hey everyone, thanks for making time; I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on the account, Diego and Priya from our SE team are here to go through a hands-on parity and onramp plan. Mark, do you want to kick with the high level goals?"

00:18 Mark Delaney: "Yeah thanks, um, main thing for Tidecrest is we run a mix of OpenAI and Anthropic endpoints today, plus a few Together models in prod for certain workloads. We're trying to consolidate to reduce vendor overhead, also cost predictability and have tight SLA controls. So we want to see parity on generation endpoints, embeddings, streaming, and tools/fn-calls. Also security is big — KMS and VPC/private options."

00:44 Diego Morales: "Got it — we'll focus on parity mapping first. Quick note: some transcriptions sometimes show 'kay vee cash' for KV cache so forgive my accent, but we'll demo how our prefix cache and kv cache behave with chat history to keep latency down."

01:02 Asha Iyer: "Our big worry is that switching will change detokenization or output formatting — we've got pipelines that expect exact JSON structure back from model calls, especially for tool outputs. How do you handle structured output?"

01:20 Priya Shah: "Great question. Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured output; our console has output validation hooks and you can pin schema in the request. There are small differences versus OpenAI’s function calling semantics — we provide a compatibility layer and sample adaptors in our SDKs. Diego will show a short example."

02:05 Diego Morales: "Okay, quick demo. I'm going to share a couple curl snippets. First, an OpenAI-style chat request and then the equivalent Redwood call. Notice the field mappings: 'messages' maps directly, 'max_tokens' becomes 'max_new_tokens' in some of our older models but our API normalizes both. Also streaming is via SSE, similar to what you know.

02:43 Diego Morales (screen): "Here's the first snippet, OpenAI: curl ... -d '{"model":"gpt-4o", "messages": [...] }'. Redwood: curl ... -d '{"model":"rw-gpt-4o", "input":"..." }' — we auto-convert chat arrays if you set 'compat_mode': true. That flag is handy for migrations."

03:27 Ben Carter: "That compat flag, is it a runtime cost? Like does it add latency or inhibit batching?"

03:38 Diego Morales: "Good callout. It's essentially a request-time shim in the control plane; no per-token execution overhead. But if you leave it on for large volumes we do recommend normalizing in your client for long-term. For POC it's fine. Batching and our GPU runtime are unaffected."

04:05 Jules Park: "Security: KMS and key rotation. We have a requirement to use our enterprise KMS (HashiCorp Vault currently). Can Redwood integrate?"

04:16 Samira Kline: "Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated customers can integrate via KMS/HSM — on Hosted we have an envelope encryption model but for Private we can use your Vault keys. Priya can follow up with the specific network and IAM steps."

04:45 Priya Shah: "I will share our 'KMS integration checklist' — it covers service accounts, RBAC, and sample terraform snippets. For the on-prem package there's an extra step for offline key material. We'll include that in the POC doc."

05:12 Mark Delaney: "On latency: our 95p for a typical 4k token request needs to be under 150ms — is that realistic?"

05:24 Diego Morales: "Depends — 4k tokens and 150ms 95p is aggressive on gen models; are you comparing to a distilled Together model or standard Anthropic?"

05:37 Mark Delaney: "Currently we use Together-medium variants for client-facing chat and some Anthropic for more guarded completions — 95p is currently around 120ms in our infra"

05:50 Diego Morales: "Okay, so two things: model selection and sequence length distribution. We can route to a lower-latency quantized variant for customer-facing chat; Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles. Also prefix/KV caching on hot sessions can cut token compute — we often see 30-50% effective latency reduction for repeated context. We'll map their exact profile in the benchmark.

06:28 Asha Iyer: "Can we run a bench against the same model versions? We want apples-to-apples."

06:34 Diego Morales: "Yes — our benchmarking runbook includes steps to load the same weights (where available) or nearest-equivalent open models, same tokenization, and a side-by-side QPS/latency trace. I'll send the runbook and an example dataset — note: some Together weights are not public so for those we'll match by capability and tokenization."

07:12 Ben Carter: "Networking — we need VPC peering and private endpoints. Will Redwood Private support our air-gapped environment?"

07:22 Samira Kline: "We have a Private on-prem package; it supports VPC peering, private endpoints, and can be deployed in an air-gapped mode with manual image transfer. There are additional steps for audit logs and we can enable an agent to push logs to your ELK. Priya will provide the infra checklist."

07:44 Jules Park: "Audit logs — we need immutable audit logs for model access and request ancestry for compliance. Is that available?"

07:52 Priya Shah: "Yes, audit logs with request metadata, model version, and token counts. For Dedicated and Private we can increase retention; we have integrations with SIEM. We'll send the SOC2 and security whitepaper as part of the security packet."

08:10 Diego Morales: "Now a quick parity gotcha: streaming chunking frequency can differ between providers. Some clients expect token-level SSE events; others expect sentence-level. We have a streaming compatibility mode and our SDKs expose a dechunker. It's a small change but worth testing in the POC.

08:40 Asha Iyer: "What about embeddings? We use both OpenAI-emb and Anthropic-emb for similarity and reranking. Are there vector differences?"

08:50 Diego Morales: "Embeddings are model-dependent — we can map to equivalent open embedding models and show similarity correlation metrics. Redwood Optimize includes evaluation tools to compute embedding drift and recommend a replacement with correlation thresholds. We'll show a small example in the runbook."

09:22 Priya Shah: "I'll also note that tokenization differences can cause small deltas in length and cost. Our SDKs include a tokenizer utility so you can get deterministic token counts during migration."

09:46 Mark Delaney: "Licensing and cost model: we want predictability — reserved capacity sounds interesting. How does that work?"

09:56 Samira Kline: "Reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) is a monthly commit; you get predictable unit economics and burst credits. We'll share example pricing tiers (GPU types, reserved QPS). For high volume teams it often pays off compared to on-demand hosted model bills."

10:24 Diego Morales: "We also have 'fallback policies' — if a primary model or region is constrained, requests can route to a compatible variant. That keeps SLAs stable. For example, if rw-gpt-4o is saturated, we'll fallback to rw-gpt-4o-quant with adjusted latency and cost."

11:02 Asha Iyer: "Is there a way to A/B test outputs during rollout? We expect to do canary testing for quality drift."

11:09 Priya Shah: "Yes — Console supports canary rollouts, traffic splits by percent, and we surface per-route evaluation metrics. You can tie prompt-sets to quality monitors so regressions trigger alerts."

11:32 Ben Carter: "Operationally, what's the onboarding timeline for a POC?"

11:38 Samira Kline: "Typical POC is 2-4 weeks. Week 1: infra setup and smoke tests; Week 2: performance run and telemetry; Week 3: iterate on prompts and rollout policy; Week 4: handoff and recommended commit. We'll adapt this to your calendar."

12:00 Mark Delaney: "We also need legal review — do you provide DPA and security addenda?"

12:07 Samira Kline: "Yes, we have standard DPA, and enterprise addenda for data residency and encryption. Priya will send the security pack which includes SOC2, ISO summaries, and our standard DPA."

12:22 Diego Morales: "Now I'll walk through a short live mapping doc I prepared — I uploaded it to the chat. It's a three-column mapping: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together field | Redwood equivalent | Notes/gotchas.

12:45 Diego Morales (reads): "Example: OpenAI 'temperature' -> Redwood 'temperature' (same), OpenAI 'stop' -> Redwood 'stop_sequences', Anthropic 'max_tokens_to_sample' -> Redwood 'max_new_tokens' mapping. Together-specific headers translate to model tags. The doc flags tokenization differences and streaming chunking as things to test."

13:30 Asha Iyer: "Nice, can we get that doc?"

13:32 Diego Morales: "I'll attach it after the call. It also includes a small compatibility shim you can drop into your client. It's in the runbook repo.

13:50 Priya Shah: "One more note on monitoring — Console gives you per-token cost breakdown, per-route latency, and token-level traces. For the POC we'll add Tidecrest's alerting targets so you can see e2e."

14:10 Mark Delaney: "For the POC we'll want a data deletion agreement and verification. Can you show proof that logs for the POC will be deleted on demand?"

14:22 Samira Kline: "Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can do per-customer retention policies and provide certs of deletion; hosted customers can request data purge too and we record the ops audit trail. We'll include the deletion procedure in the security packet."

14:44 Ben Carter: "One more practical: what sample throughput should we use for the bench? We run spikes to 1200 rps in bursts."

14:52 Diego Morales: "Send us your 95/99 traffic profile. For the bench we'll run steady-state and spike tests. Our runbook includes scripts for k6 and a simple load harness. Expect to set up a lightweight agent in your VPC to generate traffic to avoid egress variability."

15:20 Mark Delaney: "Time check — we have about 10 minutes left, let's do a short recap and explicit next steps."

15:26 Samira Kline: "Recap: we'll send pricing and reserved capacity examples; Diego shares the benchmark runbook and compatibility shim; Priya will prepare POC checklist and infra requirements; Tidecrest to confirm QPS and security playbook. POC timeline proposed week of 7/14. Any objections?"

15:45 Jules Park: "Sounds good. Also please include names/contacts for security folks and an escalation path for any data incidents."

15:52 Samira Kline: "Will do — include security contacts and a SOC escalation template."

16:00 Mark Delaney: "One ask — can you run a quick smoke test with a tiny dataset against a quantized variant to show latency improvements before we commit?"

16:08 Diego Morales: "Yes — we can provision a small instance and run a 1-hour smoke. I'll coordinate with Ben's SRE to set credentials. That can happen next week if you're available.

16:24 Samira Kline: "Okay, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark setup and the POC kickoff. Thanks everyone, great session.

End of call.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Attachments to send: parity_mapping_table.xlsx, perf_benchmark_runbook.md, security_packet_v2.pdf, reserved_capacity_pricing.xlsx, sample_compat_shim.zip.
- Tone: collaborative; strong interest in POC; primary blockers: security signoff and quantized latency verification.

References to shared artifacts in chat: links were posted to the mapping doc and runbook (links not transcribed).

Transcript end.
